blocks.text: Condo buildings in Glenwood PQ
Glenwood is a board (MLS) sub-area of the City of Port Coquitlam, not a City neighbourhood in the Official Community Plan.
The Arden — 1990 Westminster Avenue (Glenwood PQ)
A boutique condo building by Fairwind Homes, completed in fall 2018 (strata plan EPS5130), listed in Glenwood PQ.
The Sapphire — 1969 Westminster Avenue (Glenwood PQ)

The condo strata for Strata Plan BCS3110, managed by Quay Pacific Property Management (manager's AGM document); built 2008, and current listings record units as Apartment/Condo in Glenwood PQ, with a current listing recording pets as cats OK.
Portica West — 1966 Coquitlam Avenue (Glenwood PQ)

An apartment-condo building built in 1993, 50 units (building directory; an MLS sheet for the complex likewise records "Units in Dev: 50" and Strata Plan LMS916), freehold strata. The directory records its strata restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed with restrictions — the rental-restriction element of that line is void since November 24, 2022. Directory amenities: elevator, in-suite laundry, sauna/steam room; listing amenities add a clubhouse and exercise/recreation centre.
Lexford by Polygon — 2178 Prairie Avenue (Glenwood PQ)

A new condo building by Polygon (Polygon Lexford Homes Ltd.): listings show freehold strata condos built in 2026, and the developer describes over 7,000 sq ft of amenities (fitness room, yoga studio, lounge, study lounges, bike wash, kids' play area, lawn and community garden). Any unit still sold by the developer comes with the presale rules and 5% GST.
Streets, schools and transit near Glenwood PQ condos

items.t: Glenwood is a residential area on Port Coquitlam's north side. It's a real estate board name; the City's Official Community Plan doesn't name it as a neighbourhood, but it's within the City's north-side residential area.

The condos are in two small pockets: on Westminster Avenue (The Arden at 1990 and The Sapphire at 1969) and Portica West (1966 Coquitlam Avenue) in the west end, and the new Lexford building (2178 Prairie Avenue) on Prairie Avenue, where the Shaughnessy Park and Westmount Park townhouses also are. Lougheed Highway runs along the south side of north Port Coquitlam below Glenwood, and Coast Meridian Road and Lincoln Avenue are the north–south routes.
Schools: No school is confirmed inside Glenwood. Port Coquitlam schools are in School District 43 (Coquitlam), and catchments are set by address, so run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator.

Transit and recreation: TransLink buses connect north Port Coquitlam with Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express) and Port Coquitlam Station (West Coast Express). Hyde Creek Recreation Centre at 1379 Laurier Avenue is the north-side recreation centre; Evergreen Park at 3500 Cedar Drive is listed in the City Parks Directory on the north side.

blocks.text: Good to know about Glenwood PQ condos

items.t: Glenwood is a board name, not a city neighbourhood. The City's Official Community Plan does not name Glenwood as an established neighbourhood at all — it sits inside the north-side residential area — so a buyer searching City documents for "Glenwood" boundaries will find nothing.

The Arden's unit count disagrees with itself in public sources. The developer source and listing copy say 22 suites; the building directory's unit page describes the address as 16 units. The strata plan (EPS5130) settles it — pull it before quoting a per-unit figure for fees, parking or voting weight.

Two of this sub-area's condo addresses sit within a few doors of each other and are easy to confuse. The Arden (1990 Westminster Ave, 2018) and The Sapphire (1969 Westminster Ave, 2008, BCS3110) are separate stratas a decade apart in age — depreciation reports, CRF balances and bylaws are building-specific; do not carry one building's documents into the other building's deal.
Glenwood's condos and townhomes are generally newer than its houses.

Port Coquitlam bills utilities flat, not metered. Water and sewer are flat annual fees billed separately from property taxes, due March 31 — a simpler cost line to budget than metered billing elsewhere.

items.t: Glenwood PQ is in Port Coquitlam's north-central area. The City's neighbourhood profile uses the name but doesn't give boundaries, and the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 3838) doesn't name Glenwood as a neighbourhood; "Glenwood PQ" is the real estate board's name.
Schools: SD43 serves Port Coquitlam.
Maillardville sits across the municipal boundary in Coquitlam as the oldest francophone community in B.C. (a retail/cultural amenity, not PoCo jurisdiction).
Hospital: Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody — the City of Port Coquitlam has no hospital within its boundaries; Eagle Ridge is the serving acute hospital.

Rail and transit: West Coast Express runs through Port Coquitlam Station — five trains toward Waterfront (Vancouver) in the morning peak and five returning in the evening peak, weekdays only, no weekend or statutory holiday service; no West Coast Express station in any other PoCo neighbourhood.

Flooding: much of Port Coquitlam is in the Fraser and Pitt River floodplain, behind dikes; the City manages flood risk through its Official Community Plan's hazard lands rules and the regional Lower Mainland Flood Management Strategy.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Glenwood PQ

items.t: For the strata buildings, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
City of Port Coquitlam taxes and utilities: Strata units carry their own arrangements for some services — confirm on the Form B.

blocks.text: Good to know about Glenwood PQ townhomes

items.t: "Glenwood" is a real estate board name, not a City neighbourhood: the City's plan doesn't name it, and the City's profile gives no boundaries. So zoning, permits and school catchments are answered lot by lot from the zoning bylaw (No. 3630) and SD43, not from the area name.
The sub-area's stats hide the townhouses inside a combined bucket. The community attached median ($660,000) is the only honest attached figure to quote.
PoCo's entire 55+ ownership market is one apartment building with a service contract.

The West Coast Express is a weekday-only, peak-only service. Five trains each direction, no weekend or holiday service — a Glenwood townhouse bought for a downtown commute works on that schedule or not at all, and the SkyTrain business case changes nothing on any published timeline.

blocks.text: Glenwood home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

45 condos sold in Glenwood with a median price of $512,000 (the middle half sold between $426,000 and $580,000), taking a median of 36 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $576 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $408 a month. 19 townhomes sold in Glenwood with a median price of $765,000 (the middle half sold between $673,000 and $930,000), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $551 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $415 a month.

faq.a: 38, in the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® month-end figures for October 2026. Listings change every day; Jared can tell you what is available now.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Glenwood?

faq.a: With a sales ratio of 42% in October 2026, condos and townhomes in Glenwood sat in a sellers’ market. The reports read under 12% as a buyers’ market and over 20% as a sellers’ market.
faq.q: Is Glenwood a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 42 condos and townhomes sold in Glenwood over those 5 months, out of 203 in all of Port Coquitlam.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Glenwood from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: No — it is a 32-home townhouse complex at 3655 Shaughnessy St: 3–4 bedroom family townhomes, pets allowed with restrictions, no age restriction, and a build year that conflicts between sources.
faq.q: Is Shaughnessy Park a condo building?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, including the restriction element in Portica West's directory line. A strata can still restrict short-term rentals by bylaw.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Glenwood condo long-term?

faq.a: Yes, long-term — that restriction element has been void province-wide since November 24, 2022. The pets element of the same published line (pets allowed with restrictions) stands as published. Short-term rentals are a separate bylaw question — confirm on the Form B.
faq.q: Shaughnessy Park's directory line says "rentals allowed with restrictions." Can I actually rent my unit out?

faq.a: No known one anywhere in the city. PoCo's only 55+ ownership complex is Mayfair Terrace (2266 Atkins Ave) — an apartment-form strata with a mandatory Aspira service plan ($715/mo first resident / $400 second, listing-stated) — and its other 55+ name, Kew Lifestyles at Montrose, is rental. Neither counted townhouse complex here carries any age restriction.
faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse in Port Coquitlam?
What did condos in Glenwood sell for?
faq.a: From November 2025 to late October 2026, Glenwood recorded 45 condo sales at a median of $512,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Glenwood?
faq.a: The median was 36 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (4% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
